 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE RAJIV ROY
ORAL ORDER 3 21-03-2023 Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, the State and the informant.

On 21.02.2023 itself, learned counsel for the petitioner had submitted that he is withdrawing the prayer of the petitioner no. 1 Md. Abdullah Sadique @ Md. Abdulah Sadik, who is husband of the complainant/informant.

entities.text: Md. Abdullah Sadique @ Md. Abdulah Sadik
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: Permission accorded.
The petition so far as petitioner no. 1 is concerned, the same stands withdrawn.

The present petition has been preferred for quashing Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.25546 of 2015(3) dt.21-03-2023 of the order dated 01.05.2015 passed by the learned S.D.J.M., Ara in G.R.

sentences.text:
As per the prosecution story, the marriage of O.P. No. 2 was solemnized with the petitioner no. 1 on 11.12.2012 as per the Muslim Rites and cash of Rs. 2,00,000/- and some ornaments of Rs.
5,00,000/- were given but the accused persons were regularly torturing her for a four wheeler.
There is also allegation of pouring of kerosene oil and tried to burn her.

Finally, fed up with the attitude of in- laws/husband, the present complaint/F.I.R.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner no. 1 having solemnized marriage with the opposite party no. 2, he has responsibility of taking care of her and if she is aggrieved, an appropriate steps be taken by the side of husband.

So far as the present petitioner nos. 2 to 5 are concerned, the petitioner nos. 2 and 3 namely, Amir Hasan and Aaisha Khatoon respectively are parents of the petitioner no. 1 whereas the petitioner no.
4 and 5 namely Abdul Hasib @ Abdul Hasib Ansari and Mcharun Nisha respectively are brother and Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.25546 of 2015(3) dt.21-03-2023 "bhabhi".
He further submits that a bare perusal of the F.I.R. would show that the allegations that have been made are omnibus in nature inasmuch as, the demand of a four wheeler and pouring of kerosene oil has been made against all the accused persons.
It has been submitted that they have nothing to do in the day to day lickerings between the couple and only because they belong to the family, they have been roped in the case.

He has drawn attention of this Court to a case of Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs The State of Bihar decided by Hon'ble Apex Court in Cr. Appeal No. 195 of 2022 with addition to paragraph nos. 16, 17 and 18 which read as follows:
16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. State of UP & Anr.7, it was observed:-

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra & Anr. Vs. State of UP & Anr.7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
"21. It would be relevant at this stage to take note of an apt observation of this Court 2022 recorded in the matter of G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000)
3 SCC 693 wherein also in a matrimonial dispute, this Court had held Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.25546 of 2015(3) dt.21-03-2023 that the High Court should have quashed the complaint arising out of a matrimonial dispute wherein all family members had been roped into the matrimonial litigation which was quashed and set aside.

entities.text:
G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000)
3 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Their Lordships observed therein with which we entirely agree that:
"there has been an outburst of matrimonial dispute in recent times.
Marriage is a sacred ceremony, main purpose of which is to enable the young couple to settle down in life and live peacefully.

But little matrimonial skirmishes suddenly erupt which often assume serious proportions resulting in heinous crimes in which elders of the Md. Abdullah Sadique @ Md. Abdulah Sadik ... vs State Of Bihar And Anr on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149540341/
2 family are also involved with the result that those who could have counselled and brought about rapprochement are rendered helpless on their being arrayed as accused in the criminal case.

entities.text: Md. Abdullah Sadique @ Md. Abdulah Sadik ... vs State Of Bihar And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
There are many reasons which need not be mentioned here for not encouraging matrimonial litigation so that Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.25546 of 2015(3) dt.21-03-2023 the parties may ponder over their defaults and terminate the disputes amicably by mutual agreement instead of fighting it out in a court of law where it takes years and years to conclude and in that process the parties lose their "young" days in chasing their cases in different courts."

The view taken by the judges in this matter was that the courts would not encourage such disputes."
17.

Recently, in K. Subba Rao v. The State of Telangana it was also observed that:-
"6. The Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: K. Subba Rao v. The State of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out."
18.

The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.25546 of 2015(3) dt.21-03-2023 instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes, without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.
On 21.02.2013, the informant had sought adjournment for filing a counter affidavit and as such the same was adjourned for four weeks.
Today, on call, the same prayer has been made.
As prayed for, list this case after three weeks.

In the meantime, further proceeding in connection Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.25546 of 2015(3)
dt.21-03-2023 with G.R. No. 2890 of 2014 arising out of Mahila P.S. Case No. 126/2014 so far as the same relates to petitioner nos. 2, 3, 4 and 5 shall remain stayed.

(Rajiv Roy, J)
